chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha from Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The kinship (al-Rahim) is suspended from the Throne, saying: O Allah! Maintain the relationship with the one who maintains me, and cut off the relationship with the one who cuts me off.'
And it is the kinship of the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon them).
And this is the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Those who join what Allah has commanded to be joined.'
And the kinship of every person of kin.

key_terms.آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: The Progeny of Muhammad; specifically referring to the Ahl al-Bayt.
key_terms.الرَّحِمَ: Kinship/Family ties; also refers to the womb, personified here as a spiritual entity.
key_terms.الْعَرْشِ: The Throne; the highest creation, indicating the high status of kinship.
key_terms.يَصِلُونَ: They join/maintain; referring to maintaining familial or spiritual ties.
key_terms.يُوصَلَ: To be joined; what Allah has commanded to be connected.

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of kinship (Rahim) hanging from the Throne in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the metaphysical status of kinship (al-Rahim) as a supplicant hanging from the Divine Throne, emphasizing the dual obligation of maintaining ties with both the Prophet's Progeny (Ahl al-Bayt) and general relatives. This narration provides the exegetical basis for the phrase 'what Allah has ordered to be joined' in Surah Ar-Ra'd, distinguishing the specific spiritual weight of the Ahl al-Bayt's lineage while affirming the universal command of silat al-rahim. The personification of kinship underscores the active, responsive nature of familial bonds in the cosmic order.
